newsitem.title: FRANCE: French TV boss wants aid for school multimedia.
newsitem.headline: French TV boss wants aid for school multimedia.

text.p: Jean-Marie Cavada, former chairman of French educational channel La Cinquieme, said he favoured state aid to get educational multimedia products used in schools.

Speaking on Saturday at the MIP television trade fair in Cannes, Cavada said France risked running out of funds to buy such products if it overemphasised buying up-to-the-minute computers for schools at the expense of everything else.

"The same thing is happening in France as in the United States. We are spending a lot to supply hardware to schools, to the detriment of aid for the contents," he told a news conference on educational television.
He said he feared there would be a shortage of multimedia products in schools.
Cavada, who was appointed head of French television channel RFO earlier this year, added that France was currently tightening public spending, including budgets for education.
Educational television, confronted with the same pressure for profits as other thematic channels, faces competition from multimedia products.
Cavada said La Cinquieme has put television programmes on CD ROM to be viewed on personal computers.
Greg Moyer, vice chairman of American documentary channel Discovery, said educational channels must "respect the public and be clear about the mission we are following."
Advertising and sponsoring is important for educational programming, said J.D. Singh, an executive at Zee Group, an Indian educational television station.
"We must go beyond technology to favour programmes, give users the priority and facilitate acces for users," said Gerard Eymery, vice-chairman of Senior, France Telecom's multimedia unit. DT/SLA
